resources.string: This small opening in the tongue epithelium lets substances dissolved in saliva reach the tips of taste cells.
These tiny projections extend from the tips of taste cells into the pore. On sensory cells, they are where dissolved substances can be detected.
This elongated cell detects taste stimuli at its tip and signals to sensory nerve fibers farther down in the bud.
Supporting cells extend slender processes between neighboring cells and help maintain the local environment inside the bud.
Sensory nerve fibers enter the base of the bud and branch to contact taste cells. They carry taste signals toward the brain.
